settings.heading: Best Blank Shirts for DTG & DTF
settings.answer: The best blanks for DTG printing are smooth 100% ring-spun cotton tees in lighter colors — they absorb ink directly and need no white underbase. DTF is more forgiving: its film transfer bonds to cotton, polyester, and blends in any color. Both start at $4.25/unit by the pack.

settings.text: DTG needs cotton: a smooth, high-cotton ring-spun face absorbs water-based ink best — 100% cotton is the safe default.
DTF prints on anything — cotton, polyester, triblend, and dark colors all work because the design transfers off a film, not into the fibers.
Light garments are the easiest DTG wins — no white underbase needed, so color stays vivid and the hand stays soft.
For darks and poly, reach for DTF (or DTG with a pre-treat + white underbase) to keep the print opaque.
Smooth beats textured: skip heavy slubs, space-dye, and ribbing where you want crisp photo-level detail.
Buy by the pack for the real cost — blanks from $4.25/unit, dropping toward $2.92/unit by the 12-pack.

settings.question: What is the best blank shirt for DTG printing?
settings.answer: A smooth, 100% ring-spun cotton tee in a lighter color is the best blank for DTG. Cotton absorbs the water-based ink directly, ring-spun gives a tight surface for fine detail, and a light garment skips the white underbase — keeping the print vivid and the hand soft.

settings.question: Can you DTG print on polyester or blends?
settings.answer: Not well. DTG ink is designed to bond with cotton, so 100% polyester resists it and high-poly blends print dull and wash out faster. If your blank is poly or a blend, use DTF instead — its film transfer bonds to any fabric.

settings.question: What blanks work best for DTF printing?
settings.answer: Almost any blank. Because DTF transfers a design off a film with a heat-activated adhesive, it bonds to cotton, polyester, triblend, and blends in any color — lights or darks — with no pre-treatment. That makes DTF the most flexible choice when your blanks vary.

settings.question: Do I need to pre-treat shirts for DTG?
settings.answer: Only for darks. Light cotton garments can be printed straight from the pack. Dark garments need a pre-treat and a white underbase so the colors stay opaque — one reason many shops choose DTF for dark blanks instead.

settings.question: Is DTG or DTF better for small orders?
settings.answer: Both skip screens, so both are great for small runs and one-offs. DTF edges ahead when you're printing across mixed fabrics or onto dark and poly garments, while DTG gives the softest hand on light cotton tees.
